spots.cyclistIntel: An April 2024 reviewer found no bathrooms or showers, only a laundromat, and called the price outrageous. Skip it.

spots.name: Tyson Wells RV Park (Tyson Wells Market Center)
spots.priceNote: $25 per overnight, $125 per week, $225 per month plus electricity (operator's 2026 page)
spots.locationNote: 121 W Kuehn St, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. Paved streets in town, just south of Main St and Central Blvd.
spots.booking: Call. RV parking season is Oct 1 to Mar 31.
spots.cyclistIntel: The cheapest paid lot in town. It is the swap-meet grounds, and the January shows don't start until Jan 1. A Dec 2021 reviewer was living there in a tent, so tents have been accepted, but the operator doesn't say so: call first. It has toilets and hookups. Showers are unconfirmed.

spots.name: Holiday Palms RV Resort
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not published. Peak-season (Nov 1 to Apr 30) RV sites start at $65/night plus tax and electric.
spots.locationNote: 355 W Main St, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 0.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. Paved, on W Main St. The streets inside are paved.
spots.booking: Book online or call. There is an after-hours check-in box at the office door.
spots.cyclistIntel: Has a heated pool, hot tub and clean bathhouses, and is open all year. Its rules and FAQ never mention tents. Pricey for one night.

spots.name: Hassler's RV Park
spots.priceNote: unknown
spots.locationNote: 400 W Main St, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 0.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. Paved, on W Main St.
spots.booking: Call. A registration form is on the website.
spots.cyclistIntel: An adult-oriented park under new owners, with the welded 'Mechanical Zoo' sculptures. The Dyrt tags it for tents, but that is unverified.

spots.name: Hi Jolly BLM 14-Day Camping Area
spots.priceNote: FREE, 14-day limit
spots.locationNote: ~2 mi N of Main St on US-95 N — short off-route detour the wrong direction; Dome Rock is the better free pick westbound
spots.legalityNote: Legal BLM free 14-day dispersed area, ~100 sites
spots.cyclistIntel: No water — haul from town

spots.name: Q View RV Park (formerly B-10 Campground)
spots.priceNote: $25/night 'Dry Camping', plus a $2.50 booking fee, a 3% card fee and tax ($125/week). Hookup sites are $35-50.
spots.locationNote: 615 W Main St, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 0.1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. 615 W Main St in central Quartzsite, near I-10 exit 17/19. City streets.
spots.phone: (928) 927-4393 (site says this line is temporarily down; temporary number 501-691-5757)
spots.booking: Book online or call. Open 365 days.
spots.cyclistIntel: This is the baseline 'B-10 Campground' under its new name. It offers dry camping 'for non-RV folks' (a guest review quoted on its site), private hot showers that aren't coin-op, Starlink Wi-Fi, laundry and fire pits. The old B-10 had numerous tent sites. Confirm the dry site takes a tent when you book. Walking distance to everything in town.

spots.name: La Posa LTVA (North/South/West/Tyson Wash)
spots.priceNote: In season (Sept 15-Apr 15) the cheapest legal permit is the $40 short-visit permit covering any 14 consecutive days; there's no one-night rate. The long-term permit is $180. A 2024 BLM plan proposed $200/$600, but I found no sign it was adopted.
spots.locationNote: US 95 south of I-10, Quartzsite, AZ 85346. Coordinates are the Tyson Wash host station, where permits are sold. — 2.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. About 2 miles south of Quartzsite on US 95 (from I-10 exit 17), with four sub-areas. Permits are sold at the entrance host station. Dirt roads inside, reported rough after the 2026 flooding.
spots.booking: First-come; buy the permit on site or at the Yuma Field Office.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: The only Quartzsite camp with public water taps (8, though a reviewer calls the water salty, so carry drinking water), 10 vault toilets, dump and trash. Poor value for one night next to the free 14-day areas.

spots.name: Road Runner BLM 14-day camping area
spots.priceNote: Free, 14-day limit. A host issues free permits in season.
spots.locationNote: La Paz Valley Rd, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. About 6 miles south of I-10 on US 95 to milepost 99, then just west via N 53rd St / La Paz Valley Rd. Hard-packed gravel, with a steep drop-off at the road edge.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Huge and nearly empty in late Oct 2025. Go west, away from US 95 traffic. Note it's a 12-mile round trip off the westbound route.

spots.name: Desert Gardens RV Park (Sky Resorts)
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not published. RV sites start at $36/night (Good Sam).
spots.locationNote: 1240 Acacia Rd, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 185 from Casa Grande. 1240 Acacia Rd, south-west Quartzsite. City streets.
spots.booking: Book online or call. Open year-round.
spots.cyclistIntel: The Dyrt lists tent sites, but the operator site advertises full-hookup RV sites only and AllStays calls it 55+. Call first.

spots.name: Gunny's RV Park & Military Museum
spots.priceNote: unknown
spots.locationNote: Quartzsite, AZ (north side of town) — 1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 186 from Casa Grande. Paved, in town.
spots.cyclistIntel: A small RV park run by a retired Marine, with a military museum (2023 review). The Dyrt flags it as no tents. Low value for a cyclist.

spots.name: La Paz RV Park
spots.priceNote: unknown
spots.locationNote: 52301 Century, Quartzsite, AZ (about 5 mi south on US 95) — 5.8 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 188 from Casa Grande. Paved US 95 south about 5 mi.
spots.cyclistIntel: Only OSM data exists for this park. It is far off the line and not worth the detour.

spots.name: Dome Rock Mountain BLM 14-day camping area
spots.priceNote: Free. Get the free 14-day permit from the seasonal camp host.
spots.locationNote: Dome Rock Rd W, between I-10 exits 17 and 11, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 0.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 189 from Casa Grande. On the westbound route: Dome Rock Rd W (south frontage road), 3-5 miles west of town. Rocky but passable dirt. The camp host is near the entrance. Coordinates vary by source (Campendium 33.6494,-114.2715; The Dyrt 33.6409,-114.3151); the area is large.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Up to about 400 sites on hard, flat desert. Load all water in Quartzsite. Stay out of the marked gas-pipeline corridor. It's just past the segment end (mile ~176-178) and already on the road to Blythe, so it's the natural first night west of town.

spots.name: Ehrenberg–Cibola Road BLM Dispersed Camping
spots.priceNote: Free. Rangers enforce the 14-day limit.
spots.locationNote: Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, southeast of Ehrenberg, AZ 85334 — 3.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 201 from Casa Grande. From the Flying J at I-10 exit 1, take the south frontage road to Cibola Rd, which becomes Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd heading southeast. It is compacted gravel, washboarded for about 2 mi. Pull off onto open BLM desert about 3–3.5 mi from the exit.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: The free fallback on the Arizona bank if the river parks are full or you arrive after the offices close. A Nov 2024 camper said you can barely hear I-10 from here. OHVs can raise dust at times. Fill water at the Flying J or Chevron at exit 1. BLM's Sandbowl page confirms dispersed camping is available in this area.

spots.name: Villa Verde RV & Mobile Park
spots.priceNote: Unknown. $21 was reported earlier and $40 cash in 2022.
spots.locationNote: 50221 Ehrenberg-Poston Hwy, Ehrenberg, AZ 85334 — 0.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 203 from Casa Grande. Paved. I-10 exit 1, then 1/4 mi north on Poston Rd and 1/8 mi west.
spots.booking: Pay cash at the office. A 2022 camper said the office staff disappeared.
spots.cyclistIntel: A run-down mobile-home park with some RV sites. A 2021 review says there are no showers and no bathrooms. Use it only as a last resort.

spots.name: Ehrenberg Sandbowl (BLM OHV area)
spots.priceNote: Free
spots.locationNote: Off Ehrenberg/Cibola Rd, south of I-10 exit 1, Ehrenberg, AZ — 1.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 203 from Casa Grande. BLM directions: from the Ehrenberg exit take the south frontage road about 1 mi west, then turn left onto gravel Ehrenberg/Cibola Rd. The bowl itself is very soft sand, and a 2021 visitor's vehicle got stuck. Expect to push the bike.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Camping here is legal, but it's an OHV playground with dust and engine noise. Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, 3.5 mi out, is the better free choice.

spots.name: Arizona Oasis RV Resort
spots.priceNote: No tent rate published. RV sites run $63–115.
spots.locationNote: 50238 Ehrenberg-Poston Hwy, Ehrenberg, AZ 85334 — 0.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 203 from Casa Grande. Paved, at I-10 exit 1 on the Arizona riverbank.
spots.booking: Book online (RMS) or call. Check-in 12 PM, check-out 11 AM. The park is gated.
spots.cyclistIntel: An older listing description mentioned 'tent camping', but the 2026 website lists only RV sites, cabins and rentals. Call before counting on it. It has a pool, spa and river beach. The Flying J is next door.

spots.name: Levee Road BLM Dispersed Camping (Colorado River, AZ side)
spots.priceNote: Free, 14 days
spots.locationNote: Levee Rd south of Ehrenberg, AZ (across the river from McIntyre Park) — 8.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 204 from Casa Grande. 8–9 mi south of Ehrenberg on a washboard dirt levee road. One 2018 driver took 1.5 hours to cover 11 mi in an RV. There are OHVs on weekends.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Riverfront spots, but rough, trashy in places and a long dirt slog with a loaded bike (Dec 2025 review). Only worth it if you want the river. McIntyre's paid tent sites are directly across the water.

spots.name: McIntyre RV Resort (Peter McIntyre County Park)
spots.priceNote: Standard tent site from $38/night, beachfront tent site from $43 (Campspot, Nov 2026). A 30-amp RV site is $50 if you need power.
spots.locationNote: 8750 Peter D McIntyre Ave, Blythe, CA 92225 — 6.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 204 from Casa Grande. All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go south on Intake Blvd under I-10 for about 6 mi, then turn left onto Peter D McIntyre Ave (asphalt). About 6.6 mi one way.
spots.booking: Book on Campspot (campspot.com/park/mcintyre-rv-resort-blythe-ca); walk-ins welcome. Office 7am to 4pm daily, California time.
spots.cyclistIntel: About 20 tent sites on grass by the river, with newly renovated hot showers and restrooms for registered guests, a small store (ice and snacks), free Wi-Fi and a lagoon. New owners since June 1, 2025. A Campspot review from Oct 2026 and a Campendium review from Nov 2025 confirm it's open. Tent sites have no outlet.

spots.name: The Cove RV Resort (formerly Riviera RV Resort)
spots.priceNote: Tent rate by phone. RV sites are $60/night plus Blythe's 10% lodging tax.
spots.locationNote: 500 Riviera Dr, Blythe, CA 92225 — 0.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 204 from Casa Grande. Paved. Just over the Colorado River on the California side, at Riviera Dr (I-10 exit 243). It is 0.1–0.5 mi from where the bike/foot bridge and I-10 land. One reviewer called the access road 'sketchy'.
spots.booking: Call; the office is open 8am to 5pm daily, California time. The store is open 8–5 Sunday to Thursday and 8–6 Friday and Saturday. A 2020 guest got a site at 9:30 pm, but call ahead for a late arrival.
spots.cyclistIntel: The operator's own listing on The Dyrt (verified 2023) says: 'Backpacking instead of traveling by RV? We have sites to accommodate every kind of traveler, whether by bike, trailer or RV.' Campendium also tags it for tents. The 2026 website lists only RV sites, park models and day use, so confirm the tent rate. Restrooms and showers were recently renovated, and there's coin laundry, a pool and spa, Wi-Fi (new in 2026) and a store. This is the closest paid tent option to the line on the whole segment.

spots.name: Mayflower County Park (Riverside County)
spots.priceNote: Tent or dry site about $35 (2023 dry-camp rate) and possibly higher now. Sites with water and electric were $49 in Sept 2026. Booking yourself online added an $8 fee in 2023.
spots.locationNote: 4980 Colorado River Rd, Blythe, CA 92225 — 6.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 205 from Casa Grande. All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go north on Intake Blvd (US 95) about 3.3 mi, east on 6th Ave 2.5 mi, then follow Colorado River Rd 0.5 mi to its end in the park. About 6.7 mi one way.
spots.booking: Riverside County reservations online (rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches) or call the office. Check-in is reported quick and friendly. Office hours not verified, so call before arriving late. Maximum stay 14 nights.
spots.cyclistIntel: There is a separate tent and dry-camping area by the river (27 dry sites), plus 152 sites with water and electric for power. Hot showers and flush toilets, but only one bathhouse and it's far from some sites. Water spigots are everywhere, though one reviewer said the water tastes odd. Reviews from Sept and Oct 2026 confirm it's open and clean. There are no services nearby, so shop in Blythe first.

spots.name: BLM land at Wiley's Well Rd, I-10 exit 222 (beside Wiley's Well Rest Area)
spots.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit. No LTVA permit is needed because this is outside the Mule Mountain LTVA. Water and flush toilets are at the rest area 0.3 mi away, 24 h.
spots.locationNote: Wiley's Well Rd at I-10 exit 222 (north side), 15 mi west of Blythe — 0.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 226 from Casa Grande. Leave I-10 at exit 222. The Wiley's Well Rest Area sits on Wiley's Well Rd just north of the freeway. Ride a few hundred yards north on paved Wiley's Well Rd, or along the dirt powerline track parallel to I-10, and camp on open BLM desert out of sight of the road. Flat, firm ground.
spots.booking: None. You may NOT sleep inside the rest area itself: Caltrans has an 8-hour limit and no tents.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Not a documented campsite; legal by land status. The BLM surface-management map shows BLM on every side of the interchange, inside Chuckwalla National Monument, and OSM shows no solar fencing here. It is the only spot between Blythe and Chiriaco where a dry camp sits beside water and toilets. It is 10 mi past the last store (BB Travel Center, exit 232) and 50 mi before Chiriaco. Two state prisons are 3 mi south, so stay north of I-10. Check for 'closed to camping' signs. Caltrans plans a rest-area water rebuild with no dates announced.

spots.name: Wiley's Well Campground (Mule Mountain LTVA, BLM)
spots.priceNote: $40 LTVA short-visit permit, required Sept 15-Apr 15. It covers 14 consecutive days at any CA/AZ LTVA; there is no nightly rate.
spots.locationNote: Wiley's Well Rd, 9 mi south of I-10 exit 222 — 9 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 226 from Casa Grande. Exit 222, then south on Wiley's Well Rd: 3 mi paved past the Chuckwalla Valley and Ironwood state prisons, then 6 mi of graded dirt that is normally washboarded. BLM notice dated Oct 15, 2026: the road was damaged by Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel, is 'impassable for RVs and trailers', and is 4x4 only. A loaded bike will be slow, with possible walking. 18 mi round trip.
spots.booking: No reservations. Buy the permit from the camp host (not always present) or a BLM office. Tents are allowed only at designated sites within 500 ft of the vault toilet.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: A real campground with tables, fire rings, a very clean vault toilet, trash and a dump station, but NO water; bring it from the rest area 9 mi back. Coon Hollow, 3 mi further south on the same damaged road, takes the same permit. Probably not worth the detour this week.

spots.name: BLM land at Corn Springs Rd, I-10 exit 201 (south-west of the interchange)
spots.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
spots.locationNote: Corn Springs Rd / Chuckwalla Valley Rd at I-10 exit 201, 9 mi east of Desert Center — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 247 from Casa Grande. Exit 201, south side. Paved Chuckwalla Valley Rd meets Corn Springs Rd at the ramps; go a few hundred yards west of Corn Springs Rd onto BLM desert. Keep clear of the fenced Maverick Solar project north and east of the exit.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map, inside Chuckwalla National Monument). It saves the sandy 7.8-mi ride to Corn Springs campground. A dry camp: the nearest water is Wiley's Well RA, 21 mi back, or Chiriaco, 29 mi ahead. Small dirt service roads (pipeline/utility) criss-cross the area.

spots.name: Corn Springs Campground (BLM)
spots.priceNote: $6/night, first come first served, 14-day limit.
spots.locationNote: Corn Springs Rd, Chuckwalla Mountains, Desert Center, CA 92239 — 7.8 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 251 from Casa Grande. Exit 201, then south and west on Corn Springs Rd: about 7-8 mi of compacted/graded dirt with soft sandy wash crossings (a 2019 review said '4WD recommended'), climbing gently to about 1,600 ft. Condition after the October 2026 storm is unknown.
spots.booking: First come, first served: 9 sites including 1 group site, no reservations. Quiet hours 9pm-8am.
spots.cyclistIntel: A palm oasis with petroglyphs, shade ramadas, tables and grills; usually nearly empty midweek. BLM lists potable water, but a Jan 30, 2026 visitor reported 'No water available', so carry all you need. The round trip is more than 15 mi of dirt and sand. The Countri Bike rider (2016-17) considered it and went on to Chiriaco.

spots.name: BLM land south of Desert Center, I-10 exit 192
spots.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
spots.locationNote: South side of I-10 exit 192, Desert Center, CA 92239 — 0.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 257 from Casa Grande. Exit 192 (Desert Center). On the south side a rough dirt track (OSM grade 4) runs south-west across BLM land; camp a few hundred yards in. Off limits: the town lots, the Caltrans yard, and the fenced Oberon/Athos solar fields north and east of the exit.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map). Halfway between Blythe and Chiriaco. Desert Center has NO store, water or gas, so carry dinner, breakfast and water for the 19 mi to Chiriaco. Lake Tamarisk Library, 2 mi north, has a fountain only Tue/Thu/Sat in the daytime.

spots.name: BLM land north of Eagle Mountain Rd, I-10 exit 189
spots.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
spots.locationNote: Eagle Mountain Rd at I-10 exit 189, 3 mi west of Desert Center — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 260 from Casa Grande. Exit 189, then north on paved Eagle Mountain Rd. BLM desert lies on both sides just north of the interchange.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map; no solar fields mapped here). An alternative to the Desert Center exit. Dry camp.

spots.name: Red Cloud Mine Road Dispersed Camping (BLM)
spots.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
spots.locationNote: Red Cloud Mine Rd at I-10 exit 182, Desert Center, CA 92239 — 0.9 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 266 from Casa Grande. Exit 182 (Red Cloud Rd), south side. A big gravel lot sits right by I-10, and dispersed sites run along a 2.2-mi graded dirt road toward the Chuckwalla Mtns. Light washboard and dips, with soft sand in places: a 2WD van got stuck in 2022.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: The only DOCUMENTED dispersed area near the line between Blythe and Chiriaco (Campendium, 6 reviews, latest Apr 2023). Freeway noise near the lot, a high-voltage line nearby, Border Patrol around. It is 9.5 mi before the Chiriaco store, which makes it the stop if daylight runs out (sunset is about 4:45 pm PST). No water.

spots.name: Chiriaco Summit - Patton Museum Dry Camp Area
spots.priceNote: Free. There are no facilities at the sites; water and restrooms are at the Chevron food mart (open 24 h) and the coffee shop, 400 m away.
spots.locationNote: Behind the General Patton Memorial Museum, 62450 Chiriaco Rd, Chiriaco Summit, CA 92201 — 0.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 276 from Casa Grande. Exit 173. Paved to the museum, then take the dirt access road on the right side of the museum (sign: 'Welcome to Chiriaco Summit Dry Camp Area') to marked sites behind it. About 0.3 mi; the Chevron and cafe are about 400 m away.
spots.booking: First come, first served. A camp host takes your name and plate number. If you arrive after dark, set up and check in the next morning (Dec 2024 review). Maximum stay is 5-7 nights.
spots.cyclistIntel: The key camp on this segment: free, hosted, on BLM land, with marked sites including tent-only spots and stone fire rings. The NPS lists Chiriaco Summit as a camping option south of the park. Nearby: the Chevron food mart (24 h), Foster's Freeze (8am-9pm) and the coffee shop (6am-11pm). A 2021 reviewer got free water at the station. Some I-10 truck noise. A cyclist camped here in 2016 and sat in the coffee shop until it closed. A Jan 2026 reviewer described a dozen trucks parked in the area, so confirm with the host or the store. It is 68 mi from Blythe and 49 mi from the last water at Wiley's Well.

spots.name: Joshua Tree South BLM Dispersed Camping (Cottonwood Springs Rd)
spots.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
spots.locationNote: Cottonwood Springs Rd at I-10 exit 168 (north side), 4 mi west of Chiriaco Summit — 0.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 280 from Casa Grande. Exit 168, then north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd; dirt roads branch east and west just north of the freeway and are passable by car. Camp only in the BLM sections on the NPS map: east of the road between I-10 and the Edison power-line road, west of the road north of the power line, and a block further east. It is checkerboarded with private land, and the NPS says to camp 300+ ft from roadways.
spots.booking: None, first come. There are hundreds of fire-ring sites and it effectively never fills.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: 155 Campendium reviews through May 2026; a 2024 tent camper liked it, and the NPS BLM map was updated May 2026. The ground is crushed granite and sand, with little freeway noise. Mostly RVs, busier on weekends; good Verizon/T-Mobile coverage. No water: fill at Chiriaco, 4.3 mi east, or at Cottonwood, 6 mi uphill (needs the $15 park entry). This is also mile ~4 of the Mecca variant.

spots.name: Cottonwood Campground (Joshua Tree National Park)
spots.priceNote: $35/site/night (up to 6 people and 3 tents), plus a $15 per-person 7-day park entry on a bike. Group tent-only sites cost $55.
spots.locationNote: Pinto Basin Rd by the Cottonwood Visitor Center, Joshua Tree National Park — 7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 282 from Casa Grande. Exit 168, then 7 mi north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd/Pinto Basin Rd, climbing about 1,250 ft (1,750 to 3,000 ft). Slow when loaded; return the same way. The NPS describes the park's paved roads as crumbling and uneven.
spots.booking: Reservation only, year-round, on recreation.gov. There is NO cell service at the campground, so book before leaving I-10. Check-in at noon; the campground is open 24 h. Availability on the night of Nov 1: 43-50 sites free for Mon-Thu Nov 2-5 and Mon Nov 9, 26 for Sun Nov 8, but only 1 site (B16) left for each of Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7.
spots.cyclistIntel: The only campground with potable water and flush toilets between Blythe and Indio; no showers. Limit is 14 nights Oct-May. A riding group in Dec 2019 found it full, and rangers enforced the rules. The only current park alert is the Geology Tour Rd flood closure, which is not on this route. Worth the climb only for water and a proper site.

spots.name: Salton Sea SRA - Headquarters / New Camp (hike-and-bike sites)
spots.priceNote: Developed tent site $20/night; primitive $10; hookup $30. Hike-and-bike sites are listed but no fee is posted; in 2016 the host told a cyclist to take any site.
spots.locationNote: 100-225 State Park Rd, Mecca, CA 92254 — 11.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 285 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat, at -230 ft. From Mecca take 66th Ave/Lincoln St to Hwy 111 south, about 11.6 mi each way; a 2016 rider reported a wide, clean shoulder. This is on the hybrid line's CA 111 route.
spots.booking: ReserveCalifornia Oct-May; on Nov 1 it showed availability for every start date Nov 4-16. The campground is open 24 h; the visitor center 9-4.
spots.cyclistIntel: CA State Parks restrictions (checked 11/1/2026) say the main campground is open; Mecca Beach and Bombay Beach are closed. Showers and potable water are mapped at New Camp. Freight trains beside Hwy 111 run all night. It is 12 mi off the variant each way, so it only makes sense on the hybrid's Salton Sea line.

spots.name: Forsythe Equestrian Club (Hipcamp)
spots.priceNote: $75/night for the site, $88.30 with Hipcamp fees. Tent or RV site with 30A power, water and septic hookups.
spots.locationNote: Vista Santa Rosa, south of Indio/Coachella (exact address after booking) — 6.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 303 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. About 6.3 mi south of the line in Indio via Jackson St, Monroe St and Ave 54 to Vista Santa Rosa (bike router). The exact address comes after booking.
spots.booking: Hipcamp Instant Book. A 3-night minimum applies only on the Apr 2027 Coachella festival weekends.
spots.cyclistIntel: A 20-acre horse property 2.7 mi from the Coachella festival grounds, quiet at night. Expensive for one tent, but it is instant-book with showers and power. 93% recommend (20 ratings, 39 bookings).

spots.name: Lake Cahuilla Veterans Regional Park (Riverside County)
spots.priceNote: Unknown for 2026. Primitive/dry sites were about $20 in 2023; an Apr 2026 review put hookup sites at about $45 on weeknights and $75 Fri-Sun. Showers take a few quarters.
spots.locationNote: 58075 Jefferson St, La Quinta, CA 92253 — 10 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 306 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. About 10 mi south-west of central Indio by the bike router (Jackson/Monroe/Jefferson St to Avenue 58), or about 9.4 mi from the Mecca variant near Thermal (variant mile ~33). Over 10 mi, but there is no closer public campground in Indio.
spots.booking: Riverside County Parks online reservations or phone. Rarely full midweek. 14-night max. Late-arrival rules unknown.
spots.cyclistIntel: A proper campground with hot coin showers and a seasonal pool. Primitive sites sit on the concrete-lined reservoir (no swimming). The sheriff's gun range across the lake is loud by day, and it gets dusty in wind. The latest review (Apr 2026) is positive. A ~20-mi round trip, so best for a rest/shower day.

spots.name: Shadow Hills RV Resort (Desert Glamping Oasis tent spaces)
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not published. The Dyrt shows rates from $42/night, which is probably the tent space but that is not confirmed. RV sites run about $65 (Campendium, Jun 2026). Tent spaces are about 10x20 ft with an outdoor power outlet and fresh water, plus use of the resort (heated pool, hot tub, showers, laundry).
spots.locationNote: 40655 Jefferson St, Indio, CA 92203 — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 311 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. About 0.4 mi off the line where it crosses Jefferson St in north Indio, just south of I-10. Gated resort.
spots.booking: Book online with the resort's 'Book Now' button (Newbook) or by phone or office@shadowhillsrvresort.com. Office hours and late-arrival rules are not published, so call ahead. Bookings cancelled 29 days or less before arrival are not refunded.
spots.cyclistIntel: The best tent spot in the Coachella Valley: the operator's 'Ways to Stay' page and FAQ both list tent sites ('Desert Glamping Oasis' spaces by the ponds and walking trail), and tent guests get full use of the resort. It sits right on the line at the east end of the valley. Reviews mention some noise from the local road and the freeway. Good last night before the 30-mi stretch through Palm Desert and Palm Springs, where there is no on-line campground confirmed to take tents.

spots.name: Thousand Trails Palm Springs RV Resort
spots.priceNote: No tent site type is offered. Non-member RV sites were about $46/night (Campendium, Dec 2025). WiFi costs extra.
spots.locationNote: 77500 Varner Rd, Palm Desert, CA 92211 — 0.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 313 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. On Varner Rd just north of I-10 at Washington St, about 0.5 mi off the line.
spots.booking: Non-members can book nightly online. Campsite check-in is at noon; the office is open Mon-Fri 9-5. A reviewer advises arriving in daylight.
spots.cyclistIntel: Open for the season 9/15/2026-5/15/2027. Its rules allow '1 RV, 2 vehicles, and 2 tents' per site, but booking only offers RV back-in and pull-through sites. Call and ask whether a tent-only cyclist can take an RV site. It has a pool, spa, showers and laundry, and sits right on the line.

spots.name: Palm Springs Oasis RV Resort
spots.priceNote: No tent rate. Non-member RV site about $95 (Jan 2024 review).
spots.locationNote: 36100 Date Palm Dr, Cathedral City, CA 92234 — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 323 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. On Date Palm Dr in Cathedral City, about 0.4 mi off the line.
spots.booking: Thousand Trails/Encore booking; ask by phone.
spots.cyclistIntel: An Encore/Thousand Trails park. All 140 sites are full-hookup RV pads, mostly long-term guests, under the airport approach. Reviewers complain about the showers. Expect a no on tents, but it is right on the line.

spots.name: Happy Traveler RV Park (aka Happy Traveller)
spots.priceNote: No tent rate published (call for rates). RV sites about $100 (Nov 2025).
spots.locationNote: 211 W Mesquite Ave, Palm Springs, CA 92264 — 1.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 329 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. About 1.4 mi from the line through south Palm Springs streets to W Mesquite Ave. About 1.1 mi from downtown.
spots.booking: Call or email happytrav@hotmail.com. A night manager is on site.
spots.cyclistIntel: The only campground in central Palm Springs, sheltered from the valley winds. The operator lists only full-hookup RV sites and says nothing about tents. Call. Reviewers say the bathhouse is dated.

spots.name: DragonflyHill Desert Farm (Hipcamp)
spots.priceNote: $39/night, $45.93 with Hipcamp fees, for the 'Under Desert Skies' tent/RV site with power and water hookups.
spots.locationNote: 21st Ave area between Palm Springs and Desert Hot Springs (exact address after booking) — 9.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 9.6 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Long Canyon Rd/21st Ave (bike router). The last mile is a maintained dirt road. About 200-250 ft of net climbing (to about 770 ft). The host sends directions because phone GPS is often wrong.
spots.booking: Request to book (not instant). The host approves, then emails registration and waiver forms, and gives a 15-minute orientation on arrival. Full refund if you cancel 3 or more days ahead. Request at least a day or two before you arrive.
spots.cyclistIntel: The closest good tent spot to Palm Springs: hot outdoor showers, accessible porta-potties, mineral well water and an outdoor kitchen. 575 bookings, 97% recommend. The host warns of frequent high winds and near-freezing winter nights. The pool is winterized mid-Oct to April. It is a sober community farm.

spots.name: Palm Springs / Joshua Tree KOA
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not found (the KOA site blocks automated reading). A 2021 tent camper called the price 'a bit much'. RV sites ran about $91 (Jun 2025).
spots.locationNote: 70405 Dillon Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241 — 11.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 11.7 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave and Mountain View Rd to Dillon Rd (bike router). The router uses some minor desert roads, and Dillon Rd is the paved fallback. You climb about 500 ft, to roughly 1,040 ft.
spots.booking: Book with KOA online or by phone. Office hours and after-hours check-in not confirmed; staff escort guests to sites.
spots.cyclistIntel: The only conventional tent campground between Indio and Whitewater: a 287-site resort with a separate tent area (sinks shared), keypad bathhouses with private showers, a hot-spring pool and hot tub, a store and coin laundry. A Mar 2025 review mentions strong wind hitting tents. Reviews run through Mar 2026. The detour is about 23 mi round trip, so treat it as a fallback.

spots.name: Joshua Tree, Palm Springs, Coachella Adjacent (private campground, The Dyrt)
spots.priceNote: $15-25/night (The Dyrt listing).
spots.locationNote: Desert Hot Springs, Dillon Rd/Corkill Rd area (exact address on booking) — 11.1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 11.1 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and minor roads near Corkill Rd (bike router). The last roads may be sandy. Climb of about 450 ft.
spots.booking: Request to book on The Dyrt (the host approves). Call or text ahead.
spots.cyclistIntel: A fenced private desert lot with hot showers, drinking water, toilets and a small camp store, but no shade. The cheapest option in the Desert Hot Springs cluster. Rated 5.0 from 4 reviews dated 2023 to Mar 2026, so it looks active.

spots.name: Catalina Spa & RV Resort
spots.priceNote: No tent rate. RV sites from $45/night with free electricity and water (operator site, 2026).
spots.locationNote: 18800 Corkill Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241 — 10.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 10.4 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Corkill Rd (bike router). Climb of about 400 ft.
spots.booking: RV check-in is at noon. After the office closes, resort ambassadors park late arrivals until 9 pm. The manager decides which rigs are accepted.
spots.cyclistIntel: Hot-springs RV resort, open year round, under new management. The operator's pages list only RV sites and cottages; The Dyrt has a generic tent/RV tag. Call and ask whether they will take a tent.

spots.name: Windy Point x Palm Springs (Hipcamp off-grid lot)
spots.priceNote: $30.40/night, $37.63 with Hipcamp fees.
spots.locationNote: Palm Oasis Ave area, Windy Point, north Palm Springs (exact address after booking) — 0.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 337 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. Just off CA-111 at Windy Point via Overture Dr/Palm Oasis Ave, about 0.5 mi off the line. You enter over a 6-inch curb.
spots.booking: Hipcamp Instant Book. The host sends a custom wind report before your stay.
spots.cyclistIntel: A 7,500 sq ft lot with a 5-ft chain-link fence, a lockable gate, a streetlight and a picnic table. It is completely self-contained: no water, toilet, power or trash, and the host asks you to bring a portable toilet. The host warns that 'Standard free-standing tents generally don't work here' because gusts can reach gale force. Book it only when the forecast is light, and read the host's wind report. NWS shows easterly flow Nov 5-8, which can still gust at the pass mouth. Water and snacks at Windy Cove Market & Gas, 60490 Overture Dr. 98% recommend (20 ratings).

spots.name: BLM land along lower Whitewater Canyon Rd (Sand to Snow NM), unverified dispersed camping
spots.priceNote: Free, if camping is legal there.
spots.locationNote: Whitewater Canyon Rd, about 33.958-33.972 N — 5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 341 from Casa Grande. Paved road. About 1.5-2.5 mi up Whitewater Canyon Rd from Bonnie Bell, roughly 5 mi from the line. The BLM parcels are mixed in with private land, and boundaries are not marked as far as we know.
spots.booking: None. Unverified; ask BLM before relying on it.
spots.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
spots.cyclistIntel: The BLM land-status map shows BLM parcels beside the lower canyon road inside Sand to Snow National Monument. The monument page sends campers to BLM's general dispersed-camping rules but says nothing about this canyon, and no camper or rider report was found. Last resort only, for example if you miss the preserve's 4:15 pm check-in. Stay out of sight of homes and make no fire. The pass mouth is very windy.

spots.name: Whitewater Preserve campground (Wildlands Conservancy)
spots.priceNote: Free (donations appreciated).
spots.locationNote: 9160 Whitewater Canyon Rd, Whitewater, CA 92282 — 7.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 341 from Casa Grande. Paved. Leave CA-111 at Tipton Rd and follow Whitewater Cutoff to Whitewater Canyon Rd at Bonnie Bell, then 4.2 mi up the 2-lane canyon road to the preserve. That is about 6.5-9.5 mi from the line depending on the turn (the bike router gives 9.5 mi from the I-10/CA-111 junction). You climb about 1,000 ft (roughly 1,100 to 2,190 ft). Next morning, descend and get on I-10 westbound at the Whitewater exit, which is bike-legal there.
spots.booking: Reserve at least 48 h ahead with the online request form (check the campground calendar first). Walk-ins are accepted only if the campground is not full and you check in at the ranger station before 4:15 pm. The preserve is open 8 am-5 pm. Check-out 11 am. Up to 3 nights per 30 days; capacity 30 guests a day. Reservations can be cancelled for hazardous weather.
spots.cyclistIntel: The best-value stop on the segment: a free tent area with flush toilets, drinking water, a river and ponds. No fires of any kind, no generators, and no cell signal on site (signal starts about 3.5 mi down the road). The WHOLE PRESERVE WAS CLOSED SUN 11/1/2026 for hazardous weather and flood conditions, and the operator warns of more El Nino closures this winter. Confirm with whitewaterpreserve@wildlandsconservancy.org or by phone, and submit the form by about Nov 3 for a Nov 5-6 night. If you miss the 4:15 pm check-in, fall back to the Windy Point lot or to Banning KOA (about 15 mi on, with after-hours self check-in).

spots.name: Cabazon Escape (private lot, The Dyrt)
spots.priceNote: unknown (the listing shows a $1 placeholder).
spots.locationNote: 0.12-acre lot southeast of Cabazon (no street address listed) — 3.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 346 from Casa Grande. Paved local streets. About 3-3.5 mi southeast of central Cabazon via Main St, Broadway, Bonita Ave and Almond St (the bike router gives 5.5 mi from the I-10 line). At about 1,520 ft, it is lower than Cabazon.
spots.booking: Request to book on The Dyrt, or by phone or email.
spots.cyclistIntel: Listed in 2023 for tents and RVs. One of its two reviews (2023) called it 'more like a landfill' and left at once; the other, by a Dyrt staffer, praised waterfall access. It may be inactive. Call first; it is the only private listing at the Cabazon end.

spots.name: Silent Valley Club (membership RV resort)
spots.priceNote: unknown (membership resort).
spots.locationNote: Poppet Flats Rd off CA-243, south of Banning — 10.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 353 from Casa Grande. Paved but a big climb. About 9 mi south up CA-243 (San Gorgonio Ave) from Banning, then about 1 mi west on Poppet Flats Rd (10.6 mi by bike router). Net climb about 1,250 ft, to roughly 3,580 ft. Not practical on a loaded bike.
spots.booking: Membership basis; whether non-members can stay is not stated.
spots.cyclistIntel: Listed with tent sites, but it is members-only and far uphill. Included only so it is not mistaken for a nearby option.

spots.name: Banning Stagecoach KOA
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not found (koa.com blocks automated reading). Recent nightly reports, probably for RV sites: $50 (2022) and $54 (2025). Tent sites 95-99 have water only, no power.
spots.locationNote: 1455 S San Gorgonio Ave, Banning, CA 92220 — 1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 354 from Casa Grande. Paved and slightly downhill. From Ramsey St (the line) ride about 1 mi south on S San Gorgonio Ave (CA-243) under I-10. The ride back up next morning is mild, about 120 ft.
spots.booking: Book with KOA online or by phone. The office closes around 5-6 pm (2022 review), but self check-in is available after hours; registration packets are left at the office.
spots.cyclistIntel: The only campground in the Cabazon-Banning-Beaumont stretch confirmed to take tents (sites 95-99), and the safest late-arrival option in the pass. It is gravel and RV-oriented (a 2016 reviewer said it is 'really not for tent camping'), with one bathhouse. 2025-26 reviews report broken sprinklers, overgrown grass and occasional broken toilets. The pool is closed in winter, and train horns carry at night. Reviews continue through May 2026.

spots.name: Country Hills RV Park
spots.priceNote: No tent rate. Full-hookup RV site $68/night for 2 people, plus a one-time $15 resort fee (operator site, 2026). Showers take quarters.
spots.locationNote: 14711 Manzanita Park Rd, Beaumont, CA 92223 — 1.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 359 from Casa Grande. Paved. About 1.7 mi from the line in Beaumont via Pennsylvania Ave, 1st St, Michigan Ave and Roadrunner Dr, south of I-10 (bike router). The park is gated and needs a gate card.
spots.booking: Book online or by phone with a credit card; cancel at least 72 h ahead. Check-in 1 pm. Gated, so call ahead for a late arrival (a 2023 guest arranged one).
spots.cyclistIntel: The park rules are written entirely for RVs and say nothing about tents; The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is generic. Call before counting on it. Laundry is reported to cost $10 a load because of a card system.

spots.name: Noble Creek Regional Park RV campground (Beaumont-Cherry Valley Recreation and Park District)
spots.priceNote: $35/night (2022) to $35-50 (The Dyrt), for RV sites. There are 9 dry sites.
spots.locationNote: 650 W Oak Valley Pkwy, Beaumont, CA 92223 — 0.8 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 361 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. About 0.8 mi west of Beaumont Ave on Oak Valley Pkwy.
spots.booking: Required. Currently by phone or office@bcvparks.com to the district office only (Mon-Thu 8-5, Fri 8-noon). No on-site check-in was reported.
spots.cyclistIntel: The district's 2026 brochure lists 24 full-hookup, 15 half-hookup and 9 dry-camping sites. 2022 reviewers called it a parking lot with no visitor restrooms. The Dyrt shows tent sites and toilets, but no review confirms tents. A district notice says the park was closed for fire-camp operations one summer. Call.

spots.name: Bogart Regional Park campground (Cherry Valley)
spots.priceNote: $35/night (sites 1-30); pets $2/day (district fee page).
spots.locationNote: 9600 International Park Rd (Cherry Ave), Cherry Valley, CA 92223 — 2.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 362 from Casa Grande. Paved, with about 400 ft of climbing (2,785 to 3,180 ft). From the line at Beaumont Ave and Cherry Valley Blvd, ride 2.3 mi via Cherry Valley Blvd, Live Oak Ave, Vineland/Noble/Dutton St and Cherry Ave (bike router). It is about 2 mi past the segment end.
spots.booking: Book by phone or office@bcvparks.com with the district office, Mon-Thu 8-5 and Fri 8-noon. Online booking is suspended 'until further notice'. The park is open 7 am-sundown, with an attendant only Sat-Sun 8-3. The gate may be shut in the evening (a reviewer arriving after 5 pm worked the gate switch themselves). Max stay 7 nights.
spots.cyclistIntel: A shaded foothill campground run by the local park district with flush restrooms and drinking water. At 3,180 ft it runs a few degrees colder than Banning, where lows of 51-57 F are forecast. The district warns of bears, and a campfire ban was in place at its last notice. Tents were barred during COVID (a cyclist found it closed to tents in 2021), but reviewers tent-camped in Aug 2025. Call by Friday noon for a weekend night.

spots.name: Fisherman's Retreat (San Timoteo Canyon)
spots.priceNote: unknown
spots.locationNote: 32300 San Timoteo Canyon Rd, Redlands, CA 92373 — 6.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 368 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 6.3 mi from Cherry Valley Blvd/Calimesa Blvd (mile ~358.6) via Palmer Ave and San Timoteo Canyon Rd, about 785 ft downhill going in. On to Redlands is 10–11 mi via San Timoteo Canyon Rd and Alessandro Rd (470–730 ft of climbing), rejoining the line at ~mile 366–368, so the detour costs about 10 mi.
spots.booking: Unknown; call. It is a membership resort (Halo Resorts) with a separate non-member area.
spots.cyclistIntel: Private RV resort on three stocked fishing lakes, with a store, restaurant and pool. Runs as a membership park with a non-member section. The Dyrt lists showers, drinking water and toilets. Non-member nightly rates, tent policy and 2026 status are all unverified (no website, Facebook only). Long detour into the canyon.

spots.name: Yucaipa Regional Park
spots.priceNote: Tent spaces A–I. The county lists $35 Mon–Thu / $45 Fri–Sun for no-hookup sites (max 6 people), and group tent camping at $5/person plus a $20 group fee. Add a $10 non-refundable reservation fee. Seniors/veterans/military get $5 off Sun–Thu. Expect roughly $35–55 total for one person.
spots.locationNote: 33900 Oak Glen Rd, Yucaipa, CA 92399 — 4.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 370 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 4.7 mi from Calimesa Blvd (Hist US 99, mile ~360.8) via Avenue G, Wildwood Canyon Rd, Yucaipa Blvd and 5th St to Oak Glen Rd, about 570 ft of climbing. On to Redlands via Oak Glen Rd, Avenue D, 17th St and Tennessee St is about 7 mi, rejoining at ~mile 366, so the detour costs about 6 mi. Stay on paved roads; routers may suggest the Crafton Hills Ridge Trail.
spots.booking: Online only at parkreservations.sbcounty.gov, at least 24 h ahead (no same-day booking). Check-in 3 pm. If you arrive after the 5 pm closing, go straight to your site; after-hours instructions come in the confirmation email (check spam). Park hours are 7:30 am–5 pm from Oct 31, 2026 to May 2027.
spots.cyclistIntel: San Bernardino County park with 9 designated tent spaces (A–I on the park map) next to the 42-site RV loop; tents are allowed only there. The county lists hot showers and restrooms, but a 2024 reviewer in group site A said there were no showers near the tent area. Potable water, fire rings, three fishing lakes. A June 2025 reviewer camped in 'tent site E'. Elevation about 2,600 ft, and power-safety shutoffs are possible. The park also closes on the third Wednesday of November (Nov 18), after his window.

spots.name: The Unhitched Ranch (Hipcamp)
spots.priceNote: $99.51/night base for the ranch's RV/tent site (about $117 with Hipcamp fees)
spots.locationNote: Reche Canyon, Colton/Loma Linda area (exact address after booking) — 9.1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 381 from Casa Grande. Paved but hilly: about 9 mi from Barton Rd (Loma Linda, mile ~372.7) via Barton Rd and Reche Canyon Rd, a narrow two-lane canyon road with commuter traffic; about 900 ft of climbing. Leave via Reche Canyon Rd and Washington St to Colton (7.5 mi, rejoining at ~mile 375), so the detour costs about 14 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
spots.booking: Hipcamp request-to-book (the host approves). Usually one group at a time on the ranch.
spots.cyclistIntel: Family-run Clydesdale and longhorn ranch of about 40 acres, with wild burros nearby. Potable water, toilets, laundry, Wi-Fi, electric and water hookups, campfires allowed. 168 bookings, 100% recommend. Expensive for one rider, and the climb in is steep. The Hipcamp map pin is approximate.

spots.name: Riverview Ranch (Hipcamp)
spots.priceNote: $33.25/night base for the tent site (about $39 with Hipcamp fees)
spots.locationNote: Jurupa Valley near Mt. Rubidoux (exact address after booking) — 8.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 390 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 8.7 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Riverview Dr, mostly downhill (about 550 ft). Back to the Pacific Electric Trail is about 11 mi via Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave (about 650 ft up, rejoining at ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 16 mi.
spots.booking: Hipcamp instant book; arrival details come after booking.
spots.cyclistIntel: Private, shaded property near Mt. Rubidoux and the Santa Ana River. The listing promises clean bathrooms and hot showers, plus potable water, a shared fire ring, picnic tables and Wi-Fi. The tent site has 36 bookings and the listing is 95% recommended. It is next door to Rancho Jurupa and is a cheaper, quieter alternative. The map pin is approximate.

spots.name: Rancho Jurupa Regional Park
spots.priceNote: $40–55 per site per night (2025–26 reports; $55 is full hookup). No separate tent rate found.
spots.locationNote: 4800 Crestmore Rd, Jurupa Valley (Riverside), CA 92509 — 8.9 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 390 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 8.9 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Wallace St, mostly downhill (about 500 ft). To rejoin, take Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave to the Pacific Electric Trail (11 mi, about 650 ft up, ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 17 mi.
spots.booking: Reserve at rivcoparks.org or 800-234-7275. Walk-ups register at the staffed entrance gate (single-file line). Late arrivals with a reservation get gate, bathroom and laundry codes (Dec 2025 review).
spots.cyclistIntel: Large Riverside County campground on the Santa Ana River. The Lakeview side has gravel roads with water/electric sites; the Cottonwood side has paved full-hookup sites. Tents are allowed. Showers on both sides (tokens on the Lakeview side), laundry, a small store, ranger patrols. Busy and loud on weekends. A ranger warned campers to lock up bikes in 2020. rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches, so fees come from reviews.

spots.name: Harmony Heaven Campyard (Hipcamp)
spots.priceNote: $64/night base for 'Starlight', a pre-pitched 4-person safari tent (about $75 with fees). A-frame campers from $79.
spots.locationNote: Alta Loma, Rancho Cucamonga (exact address after booking) — 3.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 406 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 3.5 mi north of the Pacific Electric Trail (mile ~397.6) via Hellman Ave, Lemon Ave, Beryl St and Carnelian St, about 570 ft of climbing. Back down to the trail at Carnelian St is 4 mi (~mile 399), so the detour costs about 6 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
spots.cyclistIntel: Private half-acre 'campyard'. You sleep in the host's safari tent; no bring-your-own-tent site is listed, so ask the host. Private outdoor bathroom with a hot shower, outdoor kitchen, fire pit, pool, Wi-Fi, laundry and farm animals. 12 bookings, 100% recommend. It is the only tent-style stay near the Pacific Electric Trail between Rialto and Pomona. The map pin is approximate.

spots.name: Marshall Canyon Regional Park campground
spots.priceNote: unknown
spots.locationNote: La Verne foothills, CA 91750 (street address not verified) — 6.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 415 from Casa Grande. Paved and steep: about 6.3 mi north from Bonita Ave/White Ave in La Verne (mile ~407) into the foothills, about 1,070 ft of climbing.
spots.booking: Reservation only, through LA County Parks (reservations.lacounty.gov). It appears geared to groups. LA County regional parks are closed Mondays and Tuesdays.
spots.cyclistIntel: LA County says the park has 'forty campsites' with barbecues and a fire circle, available for reservation, next to the Marshall Canyon equestrian center. I found no details on individual bookings, fees or restrooms. Long climb. Use it only if Bonelli Bluffs and Fairplex are full.

spots.name: Fairplex RV Park (former Los Angeles/Pomona Fairplex KOA)
spots.priceNote: unknown; call (2020 reports: about $50–75 per site)
spots.locationNote: 2200 N White Ave, Pomona, CA 91768 — 1.1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 416 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat: 1.1 mi from Bonita Ave via White Ave (mile ~408). Back to Bonita Ave is 2.1 mi, so the detour costs about 2 mi.
spots.booking: Call or book online; 72-h cancellation policy. Office hours are not published.
spots.cyclistIntel: 183 full-hookup sites plus cabins beside the LA County Fairgrounds. Showers, laundry, heated pool and spa, mini-market, free Wi-Fi. As a KOA it sold tent sites with electric (2020 review), and The Dyrt and Campendium still list tent sites. It is no longer a KOA, and its own website now advertises only RV sites and cabins, so confirm tents by phone. Sites are tight and some are near traffic. The new Metro A Line stations at La Verne and Pomona (opened Sept 2025) are within a couple of miles.

spots.name: Bonelli Bluffs RV Resort & Campground
spots.priceNote: $30/night walk-in tent site for up to 2 people; +$10 per extra person (max 6); pets $2/day
spots.locationNote: 1440 Camper View Rd, San Dimas, CA 91773 — 2.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 418 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 2.6 mi from Bonita Ave (San Dimas, mile ~409) via Wheeler Ave and Puddingstone Dr to the resort entrance on Camper View Rd, about 200 ft of climbing onto the bluff. Continue via Puddingstone Dr and Walnut Ave back to Bonita Ave (3.7 mi, ~mile 411), so the detour costs about 4 mi. Avoid the park's dirt trails that routers suggest.
spots.booking: Tent sites can't be booked online; call 909-599-8355. The guest-service lobby and market are open Sun–Wed 8 am–5 pm and Thu–Sat 8 am–7 pm. A kiosk is open 24 h, with an after-hours line.
spots.cyclistIntel: The best-equipped tent option in the LA basin: walk-in grass tent sites with picnic tables and fire pits above Puddingstone Lake. Clean restrooms, showers, laundry (6 am–11 pm), two pools, a market and free Wi-Fi. The tent area is on a slope with a carry from parking, so wheel the bike in. Expect small-plane noise from Brackett Field and occasional late weekend parties. LA County day-use areas close Mon/Tue, but the resort office lists hours every day. It is 31 line-miles from the theater, and the Metro A Line San Dimas station is a few miles away.

spots.name: Gould Mesa Trail Camp (Angeles NF)
spots.priceNote: Free (no camping fee; the Adventure Pass applies only to parked vehicles)
spots.locationNote: Gabrielino Trail, Arroyo Seco, about 2 mi above the Windsor Ave/Ventura St trailhead, Altadena/La Cañada Flintridge — 6.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 443 from Casa Grande. 6.2 mi from Colorado Blvd (Pasadena, mile ~434.6): Orange Grove Blvd, Rosemont Ave and Arroyo Blvd to the Windsor Ave/Ventura St trailhead (paved, about 600 ft up), then 2 mi up the Gabrielino Trail (dirt and broken pavement, several creek crossings; bikes allowed). About 820 ft of climbing in all. From camp to the Elysian Theater is 11.9 mi.
spots.booking: First-come, first-served; no reservations. Arrive before dark because of the creek crossings (sunset about 4:55 pm).
spots.cyclistIntel: Free primitive trail camp with about 6–10 sites, tables, fire rings, a vault toilet and bear boxes. No potable water (creek only, treat it) and no showers. Steady day-hiker and mountain-bike traffic. It is not in the Eaton Fire closure, which shut the Millard and Idlehour camps through 2027, and a Feb 2026 reviewer used it. The new USFS website has no page for it, though, so call the district to confirm. Fire danger is 'Very High': no wood fires. It is the closest legal tent site to the Elysian Theater. Stay limit is 14 days.

dayAdvice.gapAdvice: The planned endpoint (mi 78.1) sits in a camping dead zone between the Gulf Shores cluster (mi 60-69) and the ferry (mi ~86). Best play: lengthen ~9 mi, catch the LAST 3:30 PM ferry from Fort Morgan (departures 8:00/10:30/1:00/3:30; bikes free, pedestrian fare ~$5-10; verify at mobilebayferry.com, (251) 540-7787) and camp at Dauphin Island Campground for $22 — you also bank the crossing against morning weather cancellation. If you can't make 3:30, call Fort Morgan RV Park (pricey) for the 8:00 AM boat, or shorten to Gulf State Park's $25 primitive loop and ride 25 mi to the 10:30 AM ferry.

Pascagoula itself has no legal campground — plan on Shepard SP 5 mi ahead in Gautier ($13 primitive) or push 17 mi to Davis Bayou. The OSM 'RV Campground' at mi 153.8 is Indian Point RV Resort (Gautier, $40/night) which is RVs-ONLY, no tents — skip it.

Diamondhead proper has no campground, and Hollywood Casino RV Park (Bay St. Louis) is RVs-only. McLeod ($35, 4-5 mi away, no backtrack) is the practical pick; Buccaneer's $20 primitive area saves $15 but costs a ~20-mi round-trip detour off the inland reroute. Decide by legs, not wallet.

Thin day. Bogalusa has NO legal camping (Cassidy Park is day-use only). Call Berry Creek from Bogalusa; if no answer or no tents, the honest choices are the 13-mi detour to Bogue Chitto SP or riding +20 to Fontainebleau's first-come tent sites ($18-27) — the latter also turns Day 5 into an easy ~52-mi cruise into New Orleans.

There is no camping in New Orleans proper — every tent option overshoots or detours: Bayou Segnette ($33+tax, cross via Algiers Point ferry then ~10 mi), St. Bernard SP ($28, 18 mi SE), KOA ($60+). For a rest day IN the city, India House Hostel (~$29-40 dorm, Mid-City, (504) 821-1904) beats the ferry-and-ride logistics and costs about the same as a Friday-night state-park site; HI New Orleans and The Quisby run ~$40+. If camping matters more than the city, book Bayou Segnette online before arrival — Friday nights fill.

Donaldsonville has NO verified tent camping. Realistic plays: (1) call B&B RV Park about pitching a tent; (2) ask at a Donaldsonville church or the police department about Crescent Park/Louisiana Square — classic Louisiana small-town move but unverified here; (3) restructure days 6-7 so the overnight lands at Port Allen (Cajun Country CG, mile ~437) or Farr Park ($10 dry camp) — both verified, ~35 route mi past Donaldsonville, which shortens Day 7 into St. Francisville to ~30 mi. Water/food resupply in Donaldsonville is good either way.

The two Tunica Hills options are a serious 14-15 mi hilly detour NW; if you want to stay on-line, either call Shelby J's about a tent spot near the bridge or push 11 mi to Jim's Camping Area on False River.

Sam Houston Jones SP is 40+ mi south — not viable.

Plan B: stop 20 mi early at the Merryville Museum cyclist camp (free, cabin possible) and ride a longer Day 13. Plan C: Kirbyville's small motel. Check Warmshowers for the Kirbyville-area host seen in journals.

HI Austin (Lakeshore Blvd) no longer appears in current listings and is believed permanently closed — Firehouse Hostel is the working hostel fallback. Warning: ACL Fest (typically Oct weekends 1-2 at Zilker, i.e. right at your Oct 8 arrival) jacks up every downtown bed — camp at McKinney Falls to stay insulated.

Johnson City proper is now a tent DESERT: Roadrunner RV Park (mi 1119.2, the old ST standby) is RV/cabin only (30A from $45, cabins $65, no tents per its own site), Johnson City RV Park is a $70-80 'boutique' RV-only park, and Flat Creek Crossing Ranch (mi 1101.6) has SUSPENDED all tent/RV camping until further notice. LBJ National Historical Park and LBJ State Park (Stonewall) are day-use, no camping. Practical plan: reserve Pedernales Falls and peel off before town, or budget-bust at Miller Creek. Cash-strapped riders have historically asked at JC churches — unverified, ask locally, never assume.

The RV-park cluster on the OSM hints is mostly useless for tents: Buckhorn Lake Resort and Guadalupe River RV Resort are big-rig luxury resorts, and Take-It-Easy (mi 1182.4) is a 55+ RV community — none confirm tents. Kerrville-Schreiner is the obvious answer; book the Saturday night early.

Foxfire Cabins (1 mi S of the SNA on the Sabinal) is cabins-only — no tent sites — and runs multi-night minimums in leaf season; treat as a splurge/bad-weather bail only. If everything at Vanderpool is somehow full, Utopia (~16 mi south, off route) has lodging, and Leakey (17 mi ahead over the big 337 climbs) has commercial camps — but on a Sunday night the private Lost Maples RV almost certainly has a $15 primitive spot; call (830) 966-3912 a few days out.

dayAdvice.bestBet: Nueces River RV and Cabin Resort (formerly Big Oak River Camp)
dayAdvice.gapAdvice: Camp Wood remains one of the friendliest cheap-camping towns on the Texas ST — three legal riverfront options within 4 miles. Resupply and top off water here: the next day westward is the famously brutal, service-free stretch toward Brackettville/Del Rio.

The mapped endpoint sits by Laughlin AFB, and the FamCamp there is restricted to military/DoD ID holders (active, guard, reserve, retired, DAV, DoD civilians) — EXCLUDED for a civilian rider, and there is no other camping at that exact point. Real choices: (a) push 8-12 extra miles through Del Rio to Hidden Valley (~$20, town services) or on to Amistad's Governors Landing ($6-10, water on site, FCFS, no showers); (b) stop 30 mi short at Fort Clark Springs; or (c) motel row in Del Rio. Whatever you pick, leave Del Rio with maximum water — Amistad campgrounds other than Governors Landing are dry, and so is the road to Comstock.

Arrive in Langtry before 5pm to load water at the visitor center. If the community center situation has changed, backtrack is impossible - so if in doubt, commit to Seminole Canyon (mile 1398.5) instead and ride a longer Day 25.

dayAdvice.gapAdvice: Budget Inn Sanderson (US 90 west side, ~$55-70) is the cheap roof fallback. Sanderson has a grocery (Stripes/Family Dollar) - resupply here, the next 71 mi to Marathon are empty.
Gage Gardens is a private hotel garden - no camping. If La Loma is full/closed, Marathon Motel's $15 tent sites are the sure thing.

The OSM 'Dispersed Camping Marfa' node at mile 1597.9 could not be verified as legal camping - likely an informal roadside pullout; skip it. El Cosmico is closed. If everything in Marfa is full (event weekend), Alpine at mile 1581 is the pressure valve.

Valentine has NO motel, store, or restaurant - carry dinner/breakfast and full water from Marfa. Sunday arrival means arrange school permission by phone Friday, or knock at the church/post office - locals are used to Southern Tier riders. Prada Marfa (mile ~1645) is an art installation, not a campsite. Fallbacks: book a Love Shak, backtrack nothing (Marfa is 36 mi behind), or grind 38 more mi to Van Horn RV Park - not recommended after a 40-mi day.

No RV park in Sierra Blanca itself takes tents (nothing verified operating). If the public park feels wrong, Sierra Blanca has budget motels (Americana Inn, ~$50-60). Load ALL water in Van Horn - the 35 mi between have zero services, and the I-10 frontage climb is exposed.

dayAdvice.bestBet: Fort Hancock Community Church (18 mi before Fabens)
dayAdvice.gapAdvice: Fabens itself has NO verified legal camping - this is the segment's real gap. Best plays: (1) shorten the day and camp at Fort Hancock Community Church (mile ~1772) with permission - the established cyclist move; (2) take a roof night: Fabens Inn, 1884 Fabens Rd near I-10, ~$79/night (reviews warn of surprise fees - confirm total price at check-in), or Fort Hancock Motel ~$60-70; (3) push ~20 more miles into El Paso's Mission Valley where motels are plentiful. Do not stealth camp in the irrigated farm strip - it is all private land near the border with heavy Border Patrol presence.

Honest gap: the Anthony/La Union/Canutillo area has no true tent campground on-route. La Viña Winery (4201 NM 28, right at the day's endpoint) is a tasting room only — no camping offered (it does host an early-Oct wine festival; don't count on pitching there). Best plays: (1) call El Paso West RV Park and confirm a tent spot; (2) push ~15 flat miles up NM 28 to Mesilla/Las Cruces — Las Cruces has an active Warmshowers community and budget motels on Picacho Ave/S Valley Dr around $55-75; (3) motels cluster at the I-10 Anthony exit (~$55-70). Some riders simply combine this into a long day to Leasburg Dam SP (44 mi ahead, $20 guaranteed legal camping).

City of Rocks SP is ~25+ mi off-corridor east — skip it. Silver City is a Continental Divide Trail gateway town and generally friendly to dusty travelers, but it has no official free hiker/biker camp in town — the visitor center or Gila Hike & Bike (local shop) are the right places to ask about current CDT-er crash options if you want to overnight in town instead.

If the free gravel lot doesn't appeal after six desert days, Lordsburg's aging I-10 motels (Econo Lodge etc.) run ~$50-70 and the KOA's tent sites ~$35 buy a hot shower and laundry before the Arizona border.

dayAdvice.gapAdvice: Honest gap: Bylas has no legal established camping. The San Carlos Apache recreation permit (~$7–10/day; buy online at sancarlos.nagfa.net or via vendors; Recreation & Wildlife Dept (928) 475-2343) covers camping only at designated tribal recreation areas — none of which are on US 70 near Bylas — so roadside camping here is NOT legal even with a permit. Realistic plays: (1) call the Recreation & Wildlife Dept in advance and ask specifically about an overnight option for a through-cyclist; (2) arrive early and ask at a church or the police station — riders are regularly hosted; (3) restructure: ride Safford→Globe (~86 mi, gentle US 70 grades) in one day as most ST riders do, or split at Apache Gold Casino RV Park/hotel (~mi 2237, 5 mi east of Globe, tribal-owned, RV $45 and tent policy inconsistent — call (928) 475-7800 range numbers or book the hotel).

The Sunset Nooks (Hipcamp tent site) — tents, showers, water
Gila County RV Park & Batting Range (downtown Globe)

Plan to stop in Globe; the extra 6 mi to Miami is trivial to make up next morning. Oak Flat CG (free, Tonto NF) is on US 60 toward Superior — the route turns NORTH on AZ 188 before it, so it is NOT relevant unless you're detouring.

Budget pick: Bermuda Flat at $8 if you carry water from Globe or the Roosevelt Lake Marina store. Schoolhouse Point was 'Temporarily Closed' as of Aug 2026. Verify Cholla's Oct 1 reopening by phone; Windy Hill (water, $25, confirmed open) is the fail-safe.

El Centro (2384–2388) has everything, including In-N-Out, McDonald's ×2, Panera, Starbucks ×3 and two libraries.
